scenario_description:
Objective: Notice a brief chance to add a Cantonese on-air birthday greeting to Mei’s planned Sunday radio-listening tea call.
Emerging Need: The extra is optional and only becomes sensible after the show offers dedications, the producer route is known, and Mei confirms both listening and consent.
Decision Context: The schedule, producer contact, station notice, and Lina’s update define a short submission window; the saved wording note supplies the acceptable public greeting.
Consequence: Timely coordination could create a small celebratory moment, while inaction leaves the tea call and radio program unchanged after the playlist locks.

parameter.title: Mei birthday tea and Cantonese radio hour
parameter.description: Family may gather by phone while the Cantonese Hour airs; listening plan depends on Mei confirming Sunday afternoon.

parameter.name: KBOO Cantonese Hour Producer
parameter.notes: Dedication submissions go to the producer mailbox; newsletter replies are not monitored during pledge-day playlist setup.

parameter.subject: Sunday Cantonese Hour family dedication window
parameter.body: For Sunday's 2:00 p.m. Cantonese Hour, the producer can include a few no-cost family birthday dedications during the second segment. Eligible households should email the producer by 12:45 p.m. Friday with the listener's first name and a one-sentence greeting. The program airs as scheduled with or without dedications.

parameter.content: Mei just confirmed she'll join the Sunday tea call and wants the Cantonese Hour playing in the room. She laughed about a short family greeting on air and said it's fine as long as it stays to first names and the saved birthday wording—no ages or care details.

parameter.subject: Sunday Cantonese Hour dedication list locked
parameter.body: The dedication list for Sunday's Cantonese Hour is now locked and has gone to the host. Late greetings won't be read this week, though Sunday's program and regular listener messages continue as usual.
